resources.string: Race the slot cars round the track and be first across the line after the chosen number of laps.
You only control the throttle. Hold your pad to speed up and let go to brake.
The skill is braking before a bend. A car that is too fast in a bend leaves the slot, loses all its speed and is put back after a moment.
Amber signs mark the bends ahead. The grip bar above your pad fills as you reach the limit: keep it out of the hatched zone in a bend. Hint says whether to ease off.
Want to take your time? Slow motion halves the speed, and Step by step turns the race turn-based: choose throttle or coast for each half second, then press Go.
Slot car racing took off in the 1960s, when cheap electric sets let anybody run tiny cars along a groove in the track.
Take turns to fish. Each angler casts once per round, and the most total weight of fish wins.
Choose a spot on the lake, then hold the button: the power meter swings out and back. Let go to cast. Farther out means deeper water and bigger, rarer fish.
Wait for a bite. Small tugs are only nibbles, so keep still. When the bobber plunges, press the button at once to hook the fish.
Hold the button to reel in and let go to ease the line. Too tight and the line snaps, too loose and the fish slips away.
When a fish gets ready to pull, a ripple and a warning show: let go and give it line. Hint tells you what to do, and Relaxed fishing gives you longer to react.
A fish that fights hard is not always the biggest. Anglers have long played a tiring fish on a loose line instead of hauling it in.
